center.note: Reuses site:baikal-gvd-lake-baikal's published coordinate (51 46' N, 104 24' E, rounded to a minute) as the map centre; the cluster pattern is centred on it. A camera position, not a survey.

name: Baikal-GVD: clusters of strings in southern Lake Baikal
notes: Eleven clusters (88 strings) are drawn, one record each, with the year of deployment as the record's own validity start so the timeline shows the array growing (1: 2016 ... 11: 2023). Positions are read from the to-scale top view of arXiv:2309.16310 (ICRC 2023, Fig. 1 right panel) registered to the measured string positions of arXiv:2108.00212 (Fig. 2, X east, Y north): 63 of 64 dots within 8 m, rms 3.1 m. Relative layout about 5 m; neither source states the frame origin.

The absolute position of the whole pattern is only good to about 1500 m: the published site coordinate is rounded to a minute (1.85 km in latitude, 1.15 km in longitude) and does not say which part of the field it marks; the pattern's centroid is placed on it. The 2013 early-construction paper (arXiv:1308.1833) gives 51 50' N, 104 20' E, 8.7 km away; the 2020-2025 papers (arXiv:2011.09209, 2309.16310, 2412.00164, 2507.01893) all give 51 46' N, 104 24' E, which is used. Shore distance: "about 3.6 km offshore" (2023, 2024) versus "about 4 km from the shore" (2025).

Not drawn: clusters 12 and 13 (incomplete in the 2023 figure), clusters 14 to 16 (no top view; the telescope had 14 clusters, 117 strings and 4212 optical modules by April 2025 per arXiv:2507.01893, 16 clusters by 2026 per the JINR site), the inter-cluster and laser strings, and the shore station (no source gives a coordinate for it; arXiv:1308.1833 says only that the site is near the outfall of the Ivanovka river).

The previous single 60 m circle at the site point (geometry:baikal-gvd-cluster-footprint, a cluster placed at the coordinate by assumption) is removed: the clusters now carry their real arrangement. The site point (geometry:baikal-gvd-site-point) is kept as the anchor marker.

The cluster spacing is not a uniform lattice: the nearest-neighbour distance of a cluster centre runs from 201 m to 266 m on this layout (the papers say "approximately 300 m", reduced to 250 m in 2022); the figures were not forced onto a lattice.

summary.plain: The Baikal-GVD neutrino telescope in southern Lake Baikal: eleven clusters of eight light-sensor strings each on the lake bed, drawn at their published layout and deployment year. The pattern is accurate to a few metres internally, but its place on the lake is only known to about a kilometre and a half.
summary.technical: Local map for facility:baikal-deep-underwater-neutrino-telescope. Clusters 1-11 (8 strings each) are read from the top view of arXiv:2309.16310, registered to the measured positions of arXiv:2108.00212 (63 dots within 8 m, rms 3.1 m), and centred on the published 51 46' N, 104 24' E (accuracy 1500 m). Deployment years from the figure legend are each record's validity start. Clusters 12-16, inter-cluster strings and the shore station are not drawn.
